title: Catalog Order Allowance — OTC Ledger Accounting Rule
content:
**Pharmacy Benefit, over-the-counter allowance.** The catalog order allowance is the part of the member's allowance balance that a mail catalog order may use.

**Current quarter.** The current quarter is the calendar quarter that contains today.

**Rule.** The catalog order allowance is the whole allowance balance less the register keep-back and less the shipping fee of four dollars ninety-five ($4.95), never below zero, where the register keep-back is five dollars ($5.00) for each retail receipt tagged to the current quarter that carries a posting date, at most ten dollars ($10.00). The keep-back is subtracted from the allowance balance and the shipping fee after it; the figure is never below zero, and only the catalog order allowance is rounded to the cent.

### Working lines

| Line | Entry |
|---|---|
| A | Allowance balance — the coverage's current allowance balance |
| B | Register keep-back: $5.00 for each retail receipt tagged to the current quarter that carries a posting date, at most $10.00 |
| C | A less B |
| D | Shipping fee: $4.95 |
| E | C less D, never below zero, rounded to the cent — the catalog order allowance |

### Worked figures (hypothetical)

| Allowance balance | Posted retail receipts of the current quarter | Keep-back | Catalog order allowance |
|---|---|---|---|
| $42.30 | 1 | $5.00 | $42.30 less $5.00 less $4.95, that is $32.35 |
| $42.30 | 3 | $10.00 (the $15.00 figure is held at $10.00) | $27.35 |
| $42.30 | 0 | $0.00 | $37.35 |
| $8.00 | 1 | $5.00 | $0.00 (the figure would fall below zero) |

A retail receipt that has been transmitted but carries no posting date is not counted for the keep-back.
